messages.subject: pairwise comparison of procD.lm regression
parts:
Hey All

I have two questions regarding pairwise comparison after procD.lm analysis. I have checked the geomorph google group for potential help, but I can't seem to find anything related to my questions.

I am comparing a gene family's abundance across diets (group variable) in a phylogeny. I am using the following code for it. Which uses SS.type="II" as my diets' group is not equal.

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(geo_functions, phy = tree) #create a dataframe that contains the data and phylogeny.

geomorph.lm<-procD.lm(geo_functions[,2] ~ as.factor(diet_type_number4), iter=999,RRPP=TRUE,effect.type = "F", SS.type = "II" ,data=gdf)

Question 1- I am getting the following warning for each of my gene-family (i.e. columns in geo_functions df).

no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Infno non-missing arguments to max; returning -Infno non-missing arguments to max; returning -Infno non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

What does this warning mean? I do not have missing data (i.e. zero values) as I am added a constant to the whole data-set to remove zero values.

Question2- After the regression, the pairwise comparison gives me the relationship between diets for each gene family. I understand that "d" is the distance between the means of two groups, and it is an absolute value. But is it possible to extract out information about the sign (positive/negative) of relationship between diets?

pw<-pairwise(geomorph.lm,groups = as.factor(gdf$diet_type_number4))
pw_summary<-summary(pw,confidence=0.95)
pw_summary2<-as.data.frame(pw_summary$summary.table)
pw_summary2$padjust<-p.adjust(pw_summary2$`Pr > d`,method="fdr")
 

Output from pairwise comparison-
> pw_summary2
            d UCL (95%)           Z Pr > d padjust diets
1:2 0.7943515 0.4472004  4.41448914  0.002  0.0060   1:2
1:3 0.2414069 0.4521401  0.41924370  0.307  0.3684   1:3
1:5 0.2984414 0.7374765 -0.01510607  0.440  0.4400   1:5
2:3 1.0357584 0.5114718  5.42394534  0.001  0.0060   2:3
2:5 0.4959101 0.7555068  0.80810250  0.206  0.3090   2:5
3:5 0.5398483 0.7392068  1.05797191  0.152  0.3040   3:5 
 

Looking forward to the reply!

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] pairwise comparison of procD.lm regression
parts:
I’ll answer the second question first.  No, you cannot have negative distances.  But show.vectors = TRUE in the summary will return the LS means and you can infer which is larger.  You can also look at the model coefficients.

Regarding the error you received I do not know exactly what caused it, but it looks like you are expecting geomorph.data.frame to understand that geo_functions is already a data frame with several columns and it should take those columns and make them separate variables in a new data frame.  Additionally, you are using as.factor in a formula.  I recommend something like the following:

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(abundance = geo_functions[,2], diet = as.factor(diet_type_number4), phy = tree)

geomorph.lm <- procD.lm(abundance ~ diet, data = gdf, …

A similar error would be produced if one thinks a data frame has a variable that is not there.  Here is an example:

> df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(5), y = rnorm(5))
> max(df$x)
[1] 0.8638125
> max(df$y)
[1] 1.766966
> max(df$z)
[1] -Inf
Warning message:
In max(df$z) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf

So, much like expecting df to have a variable $z, it appears gdf is expected to have a variable it doesn’t, because of the way you set it up.

Mike
